n254483afe16a: Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between electron and hole Fermi surfaces fundamentally reshapes this competition. This mismatch stabilizes Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov-like electron-hole pairing and drives spontaneous symmetry breaking of the EI state. The resulting symmetry breaking reconstructs the pairing phase space for SC and EI state, such that different regions of the Fermi surface complementarily support either EI or SC correlations, leading to a natural coexistence of the two orders. Notably, the emergent SC state consequently breaks rotational symmetry and develops intrinsic nematic superconductivity, even in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking fields (such as magnetic fields, spin-orbit coupling, or bare band-structure anisotropy). Our results suggest that candidate materials such as monolayer $1{\mathrm{T}}^{\ensuremath{'}}\text{\ensuremath{-}}{\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$ and the square-net semimetal NaAlSi may provide promising platforms for observing this phenomenon. More broadly, these findings reveal a unique mechanism by which competing many-body orders generate electronic nematicity, suggesting a broader route toward spontaneous anisotropic electronic states in correlated quantum materials.
n4d1723ef2a38: We track individual grains during the discharge of a quasi-2D silo and measure their instantaneous acceleration. This reveals collective deceleration waves which propagate upward through the packing, even though the outlet flow rate remains steady and follows the Beverloo law. Their characteristic frequency shows no systematic trend with aperture size and scales as $\sqrt{g/d}$. We model this scaling with a minimal stick-slip model along the dead zones, in which the relevant length scale is the grain diameter $d$. Introducing anisotropic magnetic interactions promote the formation of vertically aligned grain chains, which increase the characteristic length scale along the flow direction while leaving the transverse size nearly unchanged. This anisotropic elongation leads to a systematic decrease in wave frequency. Our results demonstrate that the internal flow is fundamentally intermittent and governed by grain-scale physics, in sharp contrast with the steady, aperture-controlled flow at the outlet.
n516eb3f630a1: Hilbert space fragmentation refers to exponential growth in the number of dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors with system size. It is taken as evidence of ergodicity breaking, since conventional symmetries generate at most a polynomial number of sectors. However, we demonstrate that generalized symmetries, including higher-form, subsystem, and gauge symmetries, can have exponentially many symmetry sectors in the tensor product basis. We further prove that noninvertible symmetries can induce additional fragmentation within individual symmetry sectors. Fragmentation in several known models arises from generalized symmetries, and the presence of exponentially many Krylov sectors therefore does not by itself imply ergodicity breaking. Finally, we show that disorder free localization arises from Krylov-restricted thermalization when sectors lack translation invariance, requiring neither ergodicity breaking nor gauge symmetry.

n0cdaf79d4774: The precise measurement of the leptonic CP-violating phase ${\ensuremath{\delta}}_{CP}$ remains one of the major open challenges in neutrino physics, as current experiments achieve only very limited accuracy. We address this issue through the lens of quantum estimation theory. A distinctive feature of neutrino oscillation experiments is that they cannot freely optimize the probe or measurement, since both are constrained by the production and detection of flavor eigenstates. We therefore examine whether the large uncertainty in ${\ensuremath{\delta}}_{CP}$ originates from intrinsic properties---either of the neutrino quantum state or of flavor measurements---or if it instead stems from experimental limitations. By comparing quantum and classical Fisher information, we demonstrate that the limited sensitivity to ${\ensuremath{\delta}}_{CP}$ originates primarily from the information content of flavor measurements. Furthermore, we show that, while targeting the second oscillation maximum, as in the $\mathrm{ESS}\ensuremath{\nu}\mathrm{SB}$ proposal, typically enhances ${\ensuremath{\delta}}_{CP}$ information, this feature in fact strongly depends on the actual values of ${\ensuremath{\delta}}_{CP}$.

n675834896a42: The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) remains poorly constrained. Using a transport-model calculation of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ in relative pseudorapidity $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}$, we find two distinct initial-state components of flow decorrelation: a long-range component driven by the global geometry of participating nucleons and a short-range component reflecting local energy-deposition fluctuations. This short-range component extends to $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|\ensuremath{\sim}4$ and can be misidentified as final-state nonflow. For isobarlike nuclei with different shapes, the calculation predicts an experimentally testable fingerprint of this component: it dilutes the deformation contribution at small $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$, so that the ${V}_{2\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}}(\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta})$ ratio between deformed and near-spherical systems, such as $\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{U}$-to-$\mathrm{Au}+\mathrm{Au}$, rises with $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}\ensuremath{\eta}|$. Separating long- and short-range flow decorrelations from nonflow gives access to the longitudinal initial structure and dynamics of the QGP.

n91de9a90c83f: We present a new ``pulsating box'' setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-$\ensuremath{\beta}$ plasmas undergoing compression-expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results could be relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in certain high-$\ensuremath{\beta}$ space and astrophysical plasmas.
n6536e5ece9bc: Ultrahigh continuous-wave intensities $(>300\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{GW}/{\mathrm{cm}}^{2})$ in high-numerical-aperture optical cavities enable applications from phase-contrast electron microscopy to ultradeep dipole traps for molecules. n14636f0267ae: We study spin-lattice relaxation times of electron spins in ${\mathrm{Er}}^{3+}:{\mathrm{CaWO}}_{4}$ coupled to a low mode-volume superconducting resonator at millikelvin temperatures in a regime where resonant phonons are cooled to near their quantum ground state. n1328698ace4e: Self-organized dynamic patterns in dense active matter are striking manifestations of nonequilibrium physics. A prominent example is the macroscopic elliptical motion observed in quasi-two-dimensional bacterial suspensions, whose physical origin has remained unresolved. Here, we examine a minimal linear-response framework in which the fluid mediates long-range feedback between run-and-tumble bacteria. Cross-film swimming combined with Jeffery reorientation produces a phase-leading nematic response to shear. Self-sustained oscillations arise only above a critical cell density and below a cutoff film thickness. Using independently measured single-cell and hydrodynamic parameters, the theory simultaneously accounts for the observed onset density and oscillation frequency while identifying film thickness as a primary control parameter for collective oscillations in confined active fluids. More broadly, our Letter illustrates how known microscopic dynamics and physical interactions can be combined into a predictive framework for emergent collective behavior.
n5746b679d329: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is indispensable for investigating interactions, collective excitations, and nonequilibrium dynamics in superconductors and correlated electron systems. However, how a small gap opening near the Fermi surface affects the spectral changes in the high-energy interband transition region remains elusive. To address this issue, we perform systematic studies of carrier relaxation dynamics in the prototype charge-density-wave (CDW) material ${\mathrm{EuAl}}_{4}$. We find that the CDW gap shrinks substantially under optical pumping. This band renormalization strongly modulates interband transitions associated with the gap edge, inducing a pronounced transient reflectivity change at the corresponding probe energies. These results establish a direct link between low-energy order-parameter dynamics and high-energy spectral responses, providing a general framework for interpreting transient signals in gapped quantum materials.

n989e88b91fb9: Coulomb interactions underpin the formation of excitons, yet their role in nonequilibrium exciton relaxation has remained unexplored. Here, using first-principles real-time Bethe-Salpeter formalism combined with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, we study the ultrafast relaxation of optically bright excitons into momentum-dark states in monolayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$. It is demonstrated that Coulomb-mediated couplings between excitonic configurations are strictly forbidden in a perfect lattice but are dynamically activated by phonon excitation. This activation enables the long-range Coulomb interaction to dominate exciton relaxation, reshaping kinetic pathways and surpassing conventional electron-phonon scattering. These findings reveal a new paradigm in which Coulomb interactions actively govern nonequilibrium exciton kinetics, while phonons act as a dynamical switch that unlocks many-body relaxation channels.
n6114f978299e: Nonequilibrium equations of state can provide an effective thermodynamiclike description of far-from-equilibrium systems. We experimentally construct such an equation for a direct energy cascade in a turbulent two-dimensional Bose gas. Our homogeneous gas is continuously driven on a large length scale and, with matching dissipation on a small length scale, exhibits a nonthermal but stationary power-law momentum distribution. Our equation of state links the cascade amplitude with the underlying scale-invariant energy flux, and can, for different drive strengths, gas densities, and interaction strengths, be recast into a universal power-law form using scalings consistent with the Gross-Pitaevskii model.
n90fb2467efe0: The local-operator entanglement (LOE) measures the classical simulability of a Heisenberg operator and is conjectured to witness many-body chaos in locally interacting systems. Using tools from free probability, we analytically compute its asymptotic value for Haar random dynamics for all R\'enyi indices. We find that to the first two orders in large dimension, for traceless operators it exactly reproduces the Page curve for random states. In contrast to higher-order out-of-time-ordered correlators, which depend on more complex operator correlations via free cumulants, the leading-order LOE is independent of the initial operator. We detail exactly how these higher-order correlations are encoded in the coefficients of the finite-size corrections. Guided by our Haar result, we argue that the long-time value of the LOE entropies in chaotic systems is robust: they depend only on a simple subsector of the hierarchy of correlations encoded by the full eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Our results therefore provide a conceptual boundary between operator simulability and higher-order scrambling diagnostics.
n0f8c2c7f4691: Measuring part of a quantum system in the midst of its evolution and acting on the result in real time is essential for numerous quantum information protocols. Neutral-atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum information processing, but their midcircuit measurement-and-feedforward cycle times have remained slow, typically exceeding 1 ms. Here, we demonstrate fast midcircuit measurement and real-time feedforward in an array of atomic qubits coupled to a high-finesse optical cavity. Local light shifts tune individual data qubits out of resonance with the cavity, shielding their coherence, while a near-resonant probe drives a selected qubit whose emission is collected with Purcell enhancement. Midcircuit measurements of four qubits with subpercent infidelity reduce the coherence of a fifth unmeasured data qubit by less than 2%. We implement real-time feedforward to correct measurement-induced phase shifts and to realize an adaptive circuit for optimal quantum-state discrimination and conditional state preparation. Our approach reduces the measurement-and-feedforward cycle time to below $100\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{\ensuremath{\mu}}\mathrm{s}$ and establishes optical cavities as a route to fast control of neutral-atom quantum systems.

n69c83a18e699: We report atomistic simulations of subcritical crack growth rates in silica glass that quantitatively align with experimental data. n913f18af04ee: We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing localized low-energy ``blip'' signatures in a liquid argon time projection chamber. We perform state-of-the-art ab initio nuclear calculations, including all relevant argon excited states with energies up to 18 MeV, to provide reliable predictions for these signals. After accounting for relevant backgrounds, we find that SBND can probe previously unexplored regions of parameter space for light dark matter.
n2e0375bae337: Open quantum spin systems offer a previously unexplored route to realizing deconfined quantum criticality. We consider a spin-$1/2$ $J\text{\ensuremath{-}}{Q}_{3}$ chain composed of an antiferromagnetic (AFM) Heisenberg exchange and a competing multispin interaction favoring a valence-bond solid (VBS) state, with each spin component coupled to an independent bosonic bath. Combining non-Abelian bosonization and renormalization-group (RG) analysis with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, we map out the phase diagram and characterize the associated phase transitions. We show that strong dissipation stabilizes an AFM phase for sub-Ohmic, Ohmic, and super-Ohmic baths. Continuous AFM-VBS transitions at finite dissipation are found upon increasing the multispin interaction in both the sub-Ohmic and Ohmic regimes, with their critical properties obtained through perturbative RG analysis and QMC simulations. In the Ohmic case, the critical point features spinon deconfinement and emergent O(4) symmetry. In the sub-Ohmic regime, the transition is controlled by a continuous family of nontrivial fixed points parameterized by the bath spectral exponent $s$ and may also exhibit spinon deconfinement provided that spinons remain deconfined in the dissipative VBS phase. Furthermore, in the super-Ohmic regime, we propose a transition from the AFM to the quasi-long-range ordered (QLRO) phase in addition to the QLRO-VBS transition.

n893802f8415d: Superparamagnetic collections of thermally fluctuating nanomagnet moments undergo a dynamic freezing known as a blocking transition upon cooling. The collective behavior becomes more complex when neighboring nanomagnets interact, and is further complicated when the constituent material of the nanomagnets has a temperature-dependent magnetization. Such a system can exhibit loss of ergodicity or the development of long-range order, and is experimentally accessible in artificial spin ice arrays, which provide an excellent framework for investigating ergodicity loss and equilibration on laboratory timescales. Using a macrospin model and a nonstandard Monte Carlo method, we describe the range of phase space that is thermally accessible, framing the problem within the context of the three relevant temperatures: the Curie temperature, the blocking temperature, and the collective ordering temperature of the nanomagnetic system. Our approach is generalizable and can be extended to a wide range of similar magnetic systems that are available for rigorous experimental tests.
n7000eebd60f2: Identifying the transition pathway for ultrafast switching between distinct antiferromagnetic orders, while holding promise to realize unprecedentedly small and fast spin devices, remains largely unexplored. Herein, we show that rectifying structure with light can serve as a powerful tool to achieve nonthermal antiferromagnetic order switching in a monolayer antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPSe}}_{3}$. By resolving the spin-phonon coupling strength, we identify a highly selective coupling of the magnetic order with a Raman-active ${\mathrm{E}}_{g}$ phonon. After resonantly pumping two degenerate infrared-active ${\mathrm{E}}_{u}$ modes, we obtain a new metastable out-of-equilibrium state holding shifted structure along the ${\mathrm{E}}_{g}$ mode. Such lattice distortion offers a sustained nonthermal driving field to trigger a phase switch from a N\'eel-type to a zigzag-type antiferromagnetic order within the coherent phonon lifetime. By varying the pumping polarization and intensity, we provide a parameter regime for realistic light-driven magnetic phase transitions. Such an ultrafast antiferromagnetism switch can be identified by pump-probe measurements of the order-parameter-like behavior in the second harmonic generation signal or absorption spectrum.
